GTA 6 JANITORS / LOCAL 6

UNION WORKERS'
AGREEMENT.

A professional network for a new kind of workforce.
The manifesto is ambitious. The terms should be clear.

ISSUE 001DRAFT FOR RATIFICATIONMEMBERSHIP: 5M+ JANITOR
ARTICLE 01

The city needs people who show up.

Everybody wants to own Vice City. Somebody has to keep it running. We are building the professional home for janitors, crews, and the server operators who hire them: work histories, clear contracts, a community feed, and a union with a visible treasury.

We believe a janitor in a virtual city deserves a real professional identity. A profile. A record of their work. Clear terms. A voice in the organization they help build.

“Quit your job. Become a GTA 6 janitor.” is the campaign. The $100K-a-year janitor is the ambition. Turning that into actual opportunities requires functioning servers, employers, funded contracts, and enforceable operating rules. It is not an available employment offer or evidence of current earnings.

Local 6 is an independent community project. Calling it a union expresses the organizing concept; this draft does not establish a legally recognized labor union, employment relationship, investment entitlement, or collective bargaining agreement.

ARTICLE 02

5,000,000 JANITOR. Your seat at the table.

The proposed membership threshold is at least 5,000,000 $JANITOR. A live implementation must verify wallet ownership and the balance of the published official mint. A typed balance, screenshot, preview card, or selected demo persona is not proof.

  • Holder membership: eligibility for the union community and proposed DAO, subject to the published qualification rules.
  • Governance: vote on union priorities, budgets, operating rules, and treasury proposals after a voting system is adopted.
  • Qualification checks: the intended design checks eligibility when joining and participating; a final snapshot or continuous-balance policy must be published before launch.
  • Below the threshold: union privileges may pause under the adopted rules. Completed-work payments and contract rights must not be erased because someone sells tokens.
  • No promise of yield: holding tokens alone does not earn a salary, guarantee rewards, verify work, or create ownership of the treasury.

The mint address, vote weighting, quorum, proposal process, delegation, and membership-review rules remain to be finalized. This frontend does not enforce membership or connect to a wallet.

ARTICLE 03

A wallet balance is not a résumé.

STATUSWHAT IT MEANSWHAT IT DOES NOT MEAN
HolderMeets the union token requirement after wallet verification.Not evidence of skill, reliability, or employment.
Verified workerIdentity and trial work reviewed; work evidence accepted.No guaranteed shifts or income.
Verified server ownerControl of a server or authorized hiring operation reviewed.No guarantee of solvency or contract payment.
Non-holderDoes not currently meet union membership requirements.Not a statement about competence or trustworthiness.

Browsing can be public. Verified union workers can share work updates. Approved server operators can post contracts under published marketplace rules, with holder status shown separately. A non-holder can still be a legitimate operator; the badge makes the distinction visible.

Verification should require evidence, human review, a stated reason for rejection, and an appeal route. No one may purchase a verified-work badge by buying more tokens. All verified labels on the current sample profiles are demonstrations.

ARTICLE 04

No shift without clear terms.

Each real job offering must specify:

  • The employer or operator, location, required role, and scope of work.
  • The schedule, expected duration, and completion deadline.
  • The exact payment amount or an explicit negotiation step, the currency, and who pays any fees.
  • The evidence required, who approves it, and the approval deadline.
  • The payment deadline, cancellation terms, and dispute route.

USD, SOL, $JANITOR, and in-game credits are different units and must never be presented interchangeably. A future escrow feature must be separately implemented and reviewed before it is advertised.

Workers can build a portfolio from approved shifts. Posts must not expose other people's personal data, private server information, or misleading evidence. Operators must not create fake jobs or self-deal with duplicate accounts to collect union rewards.

Current listings are illustrative; forms save local drafts only. Submitting a frontend draft does not notify an employer, create a contract, or secure a server slot.

ARTICLE 05

100% of collected project fees to the union.

The proposed routing policy allocates 100% of collected project fees to the union treasury. There is no separate 10% buyback-and-burn allocation in the current plan. This does not mean every trade in $JANITOR automatically pays a fee to the project.

Before fee collection starts, publish the fee source and rate, collection mechanism, treasury address, signing authority, and approval rules. Workers' contracted wages are separate from project fees and must not be silently diverted.

The intended launch pair is $JANITOR / DacityCoin, using the AudaCity token on Solana. Pairing and treasury holdings are not active merely because the asset is supported. Collected fees, DacityCoin held, DacityCoin reserved for workers and finalized DacityCoin payouts must be reported separately; holding JANITOR does not grant ownership of AudaCity or the union treasury.

Planned uses of the union fund

  • Rewards for verified, approved work.
  • Approved server development and operating expenses.
  • A disclosed reserve for continuity and quieter periods.

No spending split is adopted yet. The interface's budgeting calculator uses adjustable hypothetical inputs. Governance and treasury signers must operate under published spending limits and conflict-of-interest rules.

The live transaction view should disclose deposits, rewards, operating expenses, counterparties where appropriate, and transaction signatures. Simulated rows in this frontend are explicitly labeled and have no real signatures.

ARTICLE 06

Work first. Funding before promises.

Employer payments and union rewards are distinct. Employers owe the payments they agree to. Union rewards may supplement approved work only when the adopted program and actual treasury funds support them.

Before rewards launch, publish eligibility, evidence standards, calculation rules, caps, allocation periods, payout currency, payment schedule, and a dispute process. No formula or automatic airdrop is operational in this frontend.

A $100,000 annual salary requires roughly $8,333 per month per worker before taxes, operating costs, and other expenses. Ten such roles require a $1 million annual worker budget. A headline does not fund that budget.

The campaign target is not a guaranteed salary, token return, earnings forecast, or recommendation to leave existing employment. The supplied clips include earnings claims; they do not establish a funded salary for Local 6.

ARTICLE 07

Workers deserve a process.

  • Payment clarity: agreed scope and compensation before starting work.
  • Evidence and review: access to the reason a shift was approved or rejected.
  • Disputes: a written complaint, supporting evidence, an independent reviewer, and a stated response window.
  • Appeals: a review route for badge removal, moderation, and rejected rewards.
  • No retaliation: reporting a payment or safety concern must not itself be grounds for exclusion.
  • Privacy: minimize collected information and publish retention and deletion policies before accepting real applications.

The operator, moderators, response deadlines, governing terms, and responsible legal entity must be named before live hiring. This is a draft product policy, not individualized legal advice or a signed employment agreement.

ARTICLE 08

Our server. Built in the open.

Vice City · Union District is the planned Local 6 flagship server project. The concept includes local businesses, crews, shift evidence, and a hiring board. The map on the homepage is an original concept diagram, not an official GTA 6 map.

No live join address, game hosting, whitelist, or GTA 6 server capability is established by this website. The platform and tools must be confirmed. Any integrations, monetization, rewards, or access rules must comply with the selected platform's terms; no token-gated GTA server is promised.

Developing our own server and listing other operators are separate activities. Directory registration does not establish ownership, partnerships, availability, or approval.

ARTICLE 09

What works today.

The frontend includes a community feed, job filters, saved jobs, application and card downloads, a server directory, a concept district map, an illustrative transaction view, and a budget calculator.

Browser-local only: work updates, job drafts, server listings, likes, saved jobs, and application drafts. These are not shared with other visitors. Clearing browser storage removes them. No identity, token balance, or ownership is verified.

Still to build: wallet verification, identity checks, moderation, shared database, job publishing, notifications, contract handling, server integration, governance, fee routing, transaction indexing, and reward payouts.
